source_text: Proxime tibi, dilectissima in domino conserva, quid foeminae sanctae, matrimonio quacunque sorte adempto, sectandum sit, ut potui prosecutus sum. Nunc ad secunda consilia convertamur, respectu humanae infirmitatis, quarumdam exemplis admonentibus, quae divortio vel mariti excessu, oblata continentiae occasione, non modo abjecerunt opportunitatem tanti boni, sed ne in nubendo quidem rursum disciplinae meminisse voluerunt, ut in Domino potissimum nuberent. Itaque mihi confusus est animus, ne qui nuper te ad univiratus et viduitatis perseverantiam hortatus sum, nunc mentione nuptiarum, proclivium tibi labendi ab altioribus faciam. Quod si integre sapis, certe scis id servandum tibi esse, quod sit utilius. Quod vero difficile est, et non sine necessitatibus et hoc maximum propositum vitae supremi praesidii. Nec mihi de isto quoque referendi ad te caussae fuissent, nisi graviorem meam sollicitudinem comprehendissem. Nam quanto grandis est continentia carnis, quae viduitatem ministrat, tanto, si non sustineatur, ignoscibilis videri potest; difficilium enim facilis est venia. Quanto autem nubere in Domino perpetrabile est, uti nostrae potestatis, tanto culpabilius est non observare quod possis. Eo accedit quod Apostolus de viduis quidem et innuptis, ut ita permaneant, suadet, cum dicit: Cupio autem omnes meo exemplo perseverare.
pass_a_gloss: Next to you, dearest fellow-servant in the Lord, I have pursued as far as I could what is to be followed by a holy woman, from whom marriage has been taken away in any circumstance. Now we will turn to second thoughts, with regard to human weakness, examples of certain women warning us, who, having been given the opportunity of continence by divorce or by the death of a husband, not only rejected the opportunity of such a great good, but also did not want to remember the discipline even when marrying again, so that they might marry in the Lord above all. And so my mind is confused, lest I, who recently urged you to the perseverance of being a one-man woman and a widow, now by mentioning marriage, make it easy for you to slip away from higher things. But if you are wise in an intact way, you certainly know that you ought to keep what is more useful for you. What is difficult, and not without necessities, is also this greatest proposal of the supreme aid of life. Nor would there have been a reason for me to refer this to you, unless I had understood my own more serious concern. For as great as the continence of the flesh is, which serves widowhood, so if it is not sustained, it can seem excusable; for what is difficult has an easy pardon. But as far as it is possible to marry in the Lord, according to our power, so it is more culpable not to observe what you can. It adds to this that the Apostle advises widows and unmarried women to remain as they are, when he says: I wish all to persevere according to my example.

pass_b_english: Dearest fellow servant in the Lord, I have already laid out as best I could what a holy woman must pursue when marriage has been taken from her, no matter the circumstances. Now we must turn to a second line of counsel, prompted by human weakness and the warning example of certain women. They were given the chance for continence through divorce or a husband's death, yet they not only threw away that great good but also refused to remember the discipline even when remarrying, so that they would marry in the Lord above all (1 Corinthians 7:8). My mind is in turmoil: I who recently urged you to persevere as a one-man woman and a widow may now, by merely mentioning marriage, make it easier for you to slip from higher things. But if you are truly wise, you know you must hold to what is more useful for you. What is difficult, and not without necessities, is also this greatest proposal for the supreme safeguard of life. I would not have brought this up again unless I grasped the gravity of my concern. For as great as the continence of the flesh that serves widowhood is, its failure can seem excusable; difficult things win easy pardon. But to the extent that marrying in the Lord lies within our power, it is all the more culpable not to observe what you can. Add to this that the Apostle advises widows and the unmarried to remain as they are, saying: "I wish all to persevere according to my example" (1 Corinthians 7:8).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent translation that correctly identifies the scripture citations (1 Corinthians 7:8) which were only alluded to in the Latin. The title 'Advice to a Widow' correctly names the thought of the passage.
source: 'Cupio autem omnes meo exemplo perseverare', English: 'I wish all to persevere according to my example'
